text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today, but the bigger picture shows the stock up 12% over two weeks—a surge driven by oil price volatility and geopolitical supply concerns. Crude prices have swung sharply on news of attacks by Houthi militants on Saudi facilities, Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries (disrupting diesel supplies), and shipping threats in the Strait of Hormuz, all of which tighten global energy supply and support crude prices near $102 domestically and $126.55 globally. Today's small decline appears to be profit-taking after that strong two-week run, especially as traders briefly hoped for diplomatic progress in the Middle East.

The backdrop remains supportive for an oil major: tighter supplies from geopolitical disruption, loss of Russian refining capacity to attacks, and potential U.S. interest in alternatives like Indian refining suggest sustained crude demand and pricing power going forward.
